beats.text: You sleep better alone. About a third of people sleep apart, at least sometimes!
In a survey of two thousand Americans, one in five sometimes sleeps in another room because of their partner. Fifteen percent do it regularly.
And the ones who move out most often? Here's the surprise.
Men! Forty-five percent, versus twenty-five percent of women.
And millennials most of all: forty-three percent.
So sleeping apart isn't a breakup. Good sleep comes first. Just keep some time in bed together.

ask: TEAM ONE BED OR TWO? COMMENT.
sources: American Academy of Sleep Medicine (2023), Sleep Prioritization Survey (Atomik Research, 2,005 US adults, March 2023) – to accommodate a bed partner, 20% sleep in another room on occasion and 15% consistently; more than one-third overall; 45% of men vs 25% of women; millennials 43%, Gen X 33%, Gen Z 28%, boomers 22%.
